title: The Ghost Who Asked Us to Queue
scene: At a Halloween haunted house, a supposedly terrifying ghost surprises a visitor, then calmly reminds everyone to stand in a single line. The polite interruption turns fear into laughter.
sceneJa: ハロウィーンのお化け屋敷で、絶対に怖がらないと言っていた友人レオが、お化けに驚いてカボチャの飾りの後ろに隠れる。ところがお化けは真顔で整列をお願いしてきて、怖さが笑いに変わる。

chunks.ja: ハロウィーンのお化け屋敷で
ここには自分を怖がらせるものなんてない、と

chunks.en: A ghost appeared out of nowhere,
chunks.ja: するとお化けが突然現れて
プラスチック製のカボチャの飾りの後ろに隠れた

chunks.en: The ghost kept a straight face
chunks.ja: お化けは真顔を崩さず
「言い訳させてもらうと」とレオはささやいた
「まさか予想してなかったんだよ
お化けが接客してくるなんて」
僕はつい笑いすぎてしまったが

chunks.en: the ghost pointed at a sign
chunks.ja: お化けは看板を指さした
そこには「走らないでください」と書いてあった
それで怖さが少し和らぎ
僕らは最後まで回った
怖がるというより笑いながら

questions.question: Which split keeps the useful expression 'kept a straight face' together?
options: The ghost kept / a straight / face and said,
The ghost / kept a straight face / and said,
The ghost kept a / straight face and / said,
questions.explanation: 'Keep a straight face' means staying serious, especially when something is funny. Keep the expression as one meaning unit.

questions.question: What does 'That took the edge off' mean in this story?
options: The ghost's polite request made the situation feel less scary.
questions.explanation: 'Take the edge off' means reducing the intensity of something unpleasant. The strange politeness softened their fear.

questions.question: Why does Leo say 'In my defense'?
options: He is jokingly explaining why he jumped, even though he said he was fearless.
He is asking the ghost for a refund.
He wants the other visitors to leave the line.
questions.explanation: Leo offers a playful excuse for being startled: he expected a scary ghost, not a polite staff member.

speak: Imagine: you and a friend enter a haunted house, and something unexpected makes you laugh. Read: notice the move from confidence to surprise to relief. Chunk: say 'out of nowhere', 'kept a straight face', and 'took the edge off' as complete units. Understand: distinguish sudden appearance, a serious expression, and reduced tension. Check: answer the three questions. Speak (30 seconds): describe a sudden surprise, explain the funny detail, and say how it took the edge off. Final Read: read all six sentences aloud; pause after 'out of nowhere', use a flat voice for the ghost's polite request, and soften your voice on 'took the edge off'.
review: New: 'out of nowhere'（突然・どこからともなく）, 'kept a straight face'（真顔を保った）, 'took the edge off'（緊張・怖さを和らげた）. Reuse 'In my defense' and 'got carried away' from Lesson 108 in a Halloween setting, changing their purpose from mistaken cheering to a mock-serious excuse and uncontrollable laughter. Compared Lessons 100–113: the situation focuses on absurd customer service in a haunted attraction, with tension dissolved by deadpan humour, rather than confusion about art, sports mistakes, a festival plan, or everyday inconvenience. References: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/from-out-of-nowhere ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/straight-face ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/take-the-edge-off
